description: TYPE [TO] clause referencing a type declaration, ISO §2023:13.18.57 Format 1 (TO is the optional word, kb/Work PB889) / §2023:13.18.58 (TYPEDEF family) — a COBOL-2002 introduction. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): the 1985 TYPE clause is the report writer's alone ('The TYPE clause specifies the particular type of report group that is described by this entry', §1985:XIII.3.20.1), the 1985 data description entry's Format 1 has no TYPE clause (§1985:VI.5.3.3 SR2: 'The remaining clauses may be written in any order'), and TYPEDEF is no 1985 reserved word (§1985:IV.8 runs TYPE, UNIT: its rows '| OCCURS | RECORD | SIGN | TYPE |' and '| OFF | REDEFINES | SORT | UNIT |'); §2002:13.16.55 reads 'The TYPE clause in a data description entry specifies that the data description of the entry is specified by a type declaration' (§2002:13.16.55.3 GR1: 'The effect of the TYPE clause is as though the data description identified by type-name-1 had been coded in place of the TYPE clause'), and §2002:F.2 states the change, its item 137: 'The TYPEDEF clause identifies a type declaration which creates a user-defined type. The TYPE clause is used to apply this user-defined type to the description of a data item.' §2014:13.18.57 and §2014:13.18.57.3 GR1 carry it, so 2014 = 2023 (the former 2023-only gate was wrong; DEVLOG 582). LIVE (data-model D17, weak-TYPE spine).
